title: Star motif — eight point
subtitle: An eight-pointed star worked in the round with pointed spike sections
excerpt: Eight evenly spaced points radiate from the centre ring, each built by stepping up to a treble tip then decreasing back down. Four rounds in DK cotton produce a 12 cm star with a compact centre and sharp outer points suitable for Christmas decorations and applique panels.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 4 (1889), eight-point star chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886).
heroPrompt: An eight-point crochet star motif in deep red DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Eight sharp points radiating from a flat centre, 12 cm tip to tip.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished eight-point star measures 12 cm tip to tip in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Star motif — eight point
chartDefinition.caption: Eight spike sections. Foundation round sets 8 groups of stitches separated by ch-2 valleys. Point round builds each spike. Border round defines the outline.

glossaryTerms.definition: Using progressively taller stitches — dc, htr, tr — along a sequence to create a sloped edge, then reversing the order to slope back down. Used to build each point of a star motif.

content.text: to form each of the eight points: dc at the base, htr on the slope, tr at the tip. The tip chain gives the sharpest point. Valley slip stitches pull the indentations tight between each point.

Four rounds give a 12 cm star. The third round adds one extra stitch per side on each point for a slightly longer point; the border round traces the outline in dc. Block with all 16 tip-and-valley positions pinned.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 10 g of DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Blocking mat and 16 pins.

content.text: Magic ring. *3 dc into ring. Ch 2.* Rep 8 times. Sl st to first dc. Pull ring closed. (24 dc, 8 ch-2 valleys.)
*1 dc, 1 htr, 1 tr, ch 2 (tip), 1 tr, 1 htr, 1 dc. Sl st into valley ch-2 sp.* Rep from * 7 more times. (8 points made.)
*2 dc, 1 htr, 1 tr, ch 2 (tip), 1 tr, 1 htr, 2 dc. Sl st into valley.* Rep from * around. (8 deeper points.)
Work dc along each side of each point, ch 1 at each tip, sl st at each valley. Fasten off.

The advanced snowflake uses a similar eight-section construction but replaces the solid spikes with lace chain arches. Or try the kaleidoscope round for a circular motif with radiating colour sections.
